newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures firm on dollar's advance.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures firm on dollar's advance.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed firmer in quiet trade on Tuesday, helped by the dollar's advance, traders said.

"It was quiet. Prices firmed in line with the dollar but few were willing to build positions," said one trader, citing the metal's unimpressive performance on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Monday.
The benchmark June contract gained 0.4 yen to 186.8 yen, while the April advanced 1.1 yen to 188.3 yen. Others ranged from 0.9 yen lower to 1.0 yen firmer. Estimated volume was 2,175 lots.
In London overnight, three-month aluminium finished up $2 at $1,502 a tonne, while copper was up $13 at $2,315 per tonne.
